title: Rabbi Yehudah bar Titus
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: A student of Rabbi Acha, in whose name he reported [teachings], [as in] Berakhot ch. 3 halakhah 4, Sukkah ch. 8 halakhah 8; and in Shabbat ch. 13 halakhah 2, [there is] R. Y. bar Titus, Rabbi Yehudah ben Pazi, Shimon bar Ba, in the name of Rabbi Yochanan. And in Bikkurim ch. 3, end of halakhah 3, [it says] that he needed to go to Rome, and they ordained him temporarily on condition that he return to the Land of Israel, and Rabbi Chama called him Yehudah bar Titas. Of those who speak in his name, we find that the Rabbanan of Caesarea said [a teaching] in his name, as in Gittin ch. 5 halakhah 10, Avodah Zarah ch. 2 halakhah 3. And in Knesset HaGedolah on Yoreh De’ah, he cites in the name of the book Tamim De'im that it should read Rabbi Yehudah ben Antigonus, for how is it possible for an Israelite to be called by the name Titus? It seems more likely that it should read R. Y. bar Sitos, as in Shevi'it, end of ch. 5, and that the samekh was mistakenly turned into a tet.[^2][^3]

notes.text: The proofread Hebrew heading has בר טיטוס (bar Titus), while the catalog name has בר מימוס (bar Mimos). Hyman also gives the forms Titas and Sitos.

כנ״הג ביו״ד abbreviates Knesset HaGedolah on Yoreh De’ah; see the [National Library of Israel’s Benveniste catalog](https://www.nli.org.il/en/a-topic/987007300354705171). תמים דעים is the work Tamim De’im. The proposed Sitos reading abbreviates the personal name to י, “Y.”
Hyman prints Sukkah chapter 8, halakhah 8, although Sukkah has no eighth chapter. This reference remains unresolved. His Shabbat locator is פ״יג, chapter 13.
